task.title: Resolve schedule provenance through the developer CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/823 by exposing exact provenance from a task to its schedule as deterministic read-only JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Add vela-dev schedule task for one validated exact task identity.
Return the complete existing schedule projection or null for a valid unbound task.
Fail closed on malformed or ambiguous persisted bindings without partial output or storage creation.
Keep lookup separate from schedule mutation, task lifecycle, dispatch, provider, tool, and execution authority.

attempts.summary: Established RED task provenance CLI behavior.
attempts.diagnostic: The first CLI integration test failed because task was not a recognized schedule subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added bound, unbound, escaped, empty-ID, missing-storage, and ambiguous-corruption integration coverage.

attempts.diagnostic: The typed reverse lookup existed only in the kernel and the inventory JSON mapping had begun to duplicate schedule projection logic.
attempts.patch: Validated TaskId before storage access, routed it through ScheduleStore::find_by_task_id, and extracted the already-duplicated schedule JSON mapping.

attempts.summary: Fixed the substantive review finding with focused RED-to-GREEN evidence.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit found that the ambiguity test inserted escaped quotation marks inside a SQL parameter, producing invalid JSON and exercising decode failure instead of AmbiguousTaskBinding.
attempts.patch: Replaced the fixture with valid duplicate-binding JSON, confirmed the test failed when ambiguity handling was disabled and passed when restored, resolved the thread, and completed exact-head review.

outcome.summary: Operators can resolve exact task schedule provenance while absent, malformed, and ambiguous evidence remain distinct and fail closed where required.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-dev --test cli task_schedule

lessons: Test fixtures must reach the intended typed failure path; malformed setup data can make a negative test pass for the wrong reason.
A review finding about test reachability deserves explicit RED-to-GREEN proof, not only a corrected literal.
Return null for a valid unbound task but fail closed when corrupted state binds one task to multiple schedules.
Extract a shared projection only after two real CLI paths need the same complete schedule shape.
After fixing a reviewed commit, require substantive review of the exact new head rather than accepting a rate-limit success status.
